findings.message: The change loosens the type of the global `--_fs-base` font-size token from `<length>` to `*`. That affects every `--fs-*` size in the library, and nothing in the Legend work explains why it was needed. An invalid override now breaks every derived font size instead of falling back to 1rem. The diff changes `@property --_fs-base { syntax: "<length>"` to `syntax: "*"`. Every token from `--fs-2xs` to `--fs-6xl` is built as `calc(var(--_fs-base) * pow(...))` (variables.css:76-86). With the `<length>` type, a non-length override such as `--_fs-base: 16` or `large` was rejected and the 1rem initial value was kept. With `*` the value is substituted as written, so the `calc` is invalid wherever it is used. Relative overrides such as `em` are also no longer resolved once at the root; they pass down as unresolved text. No Legend file reads `--_fs-base`.

Legend's default layout has changed: it used to be a full-width, centred row and is now an `inline-flex` column aligned to `flex-start`. Anyone rendering `<Legend>` directly loses the centring with no warning. Only the in-repo charts were updated to add `alignSelf="center"`. The old root was `<Flex role="list" ... justifyContent="center" gap="lg">`. The new root is `<Flex {...rootFlexProps} direction="column" alignItems="flex-start" display="inline-flex" ...>` with no `justifyContent`. The JSDoc line "Renders a horizontally centered legend" was removed. bar-chart/src/index.tsx:444,619 and line-chart/src/index.tsx:491 now pass `alignSelf="center"` to compensate. Snapshot changes confirm the old `justify-content:center` is gone.

The new orientation test says it checks that items stack vertically, but it only counts list items. It would still pass if `orientation="vertical"` were ignored and the items were laid out in a row. `verticalOrientation` asserts only `assume(list).exists()` and `assume(items.length).equals(3)`. It never checks `flex-direction`, element positions or bounding boxes. A horizontal list also has three `listitem`s.

The new label test's assertions call `exists()` on Locator objects, which are always non-null. The test therefore can't fail if the accessible name or the visible label is missing. `const list = locator.getByRole('list', { name: 'Sales by product' }); ... assume(list).exists(); assume(label).exists();` A vitest-browser locator is a lazy query object, and nothing awaits it, calls `.element()` or uses `expect.element(...).toBeInTheDocument()`. So `assume(...).exists()` is true whatever the DOM contains.

The change rewrites the expected output of existing locked tests to match the new rendering: the BarChart, LineChart and Legend node snapshots, plus 11 visual screenshot baselines. Those regressions now pass by definition instead of being judged against the old output. The diff replaces the existing snapshot entries for bar-chart multi-series, horizontal-multi-series, rtl-multi-series and rtl-horizontal-multi-series. It does the same for line-chart browser-usage, city-temperature, legend and multiple-series, and for legend single-series and multi-series. It also updates PNG baselines under bar-chart/test/__screenshots__ and line-chart/test/__screenshots__. acceptance.md says the baseline's tests are the locked acceptance tests. No packet entry records who approved the new expectations.

The `size` prop is covered only by a snapshot of the `data-size` attribute. No test checks that sizes actually change the rendered font or swatch size, so a broken CSS selector would go unnoticed. The `#size` test is `expect(renderToString(<LegendSizeChartExample />)).toMatchSnapshot()`, and that snapshot (generated from the new code) shows only `data-size="sm|md|lg|xl"`. The CSS in index.module.css (`.root[data-size=...] { font-size }`, `.root .swatch { width: 1em }`) is never exercised by a computed-style assertion.

When `label` is set, screen readers announce it twice: once as the visible text and again as the list's `aria-label`. The visible text is not programmatically tied to the list. `{label ? <Text className={styles.label}>{label}</Text> : null}` is followed by `<Flex role="list" aria-label={label ?? 'Chart legend'}>`. Giving the label an id and pointing `aria-labelledby` at it would name the list without repeating the text.

LegendProps now accepts every Flex/Box prop and spreads them onto the outer wrapper rather than the list. ARIA props a caller passes, such as `aria-label` or `role`, land on a div with no role and don't rename the list. `extends Omit<FlexProps<'div'>, 'children' | 'direction' | 'display' | 'alignItems' | 'gap'>` and `<Flex {...rootFlexProps} ...>` on the wrapper. The list's `aria-label` is hard-wired to `label ?? 'Chart legend'` on the inner Flex.

The `useMemo` around the legend items adds complexity but saves little. Callers usually pass an inline `series` array, which changes identity on every render, and mapping a handful of items is cheap. `const items = useMemo(function getLegendItems() { return series.map(...) }, [series]);` The examples and the charts pass `series` arrays straight through, for example `const series = [...]` inside `LegendVerticalExample`, which is recreated on each render.
